extracted.intended_audience: journalists and newsrooms interested in solutions journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory guidance for journalists and newsrooms on producing solutions journalism: rigorous, evidence-based reporting that investigates responses to societal problems and explains what works (and what doesn't).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous, evidence-based reporting that focuses on responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous and evidence-based reporting that primarily focuses on responses to societal problems. We define solutions journalism as a practice that investigates and explains, in a critical and clear-eyed way, how people try to solve widely shared problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By adding rigorous, evidence-based coverage of solutions, journalists can tell the whole story. The guide is presented as a comprehensive resource to explore the concept and why it matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand newsworthiness to include what works
rubrics_metrics.description: While journalists usually define news as what's gone wrong, solutions journalism tries to expand this notion by emphasising that what works is also newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame coverage so that responses and effective practices are treated as newsworthy subjects alongside problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide actionable insights, not just inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions Journalism doesn't just offer feel-good stories; it provides actionable insights that can help you and your community handle pressing issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid surface-level inspiration; aim to deliver meaningful knowledge and practical takeaways that readers can use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back claims with persistent evidence (data and qualitative results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions Journalism is all about providing you with data and qualitative results, so you can see for yourself the effectiveness (or lack thereof) of solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on empirical evidence rather than unclear intentions. Use both quantitative data and qualitative outcomes to assess solution effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss limitations and avoid hype
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions Journalism discusses the limitations of responses, driving clear of the hype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the full picture by acknowledging constraints, trade-offs, scope, and contexts where a solution may not work, rather than presenting overly optimistic or promotional accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goal is to inform, not to make people feel good
rubrics_metrics.description: "The primary goal of solutions journalism is not to make people feel good, although it's great impact when that happens. Its goal is to inform people better".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise accuracy, nuance, and critical assessment over uplifting or feel-good framing; impact in mood is secondary to informing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate and explain how people try to solve widely shared problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigates and explains, in a critical and clear-eyed way, how people try to solve widely shared problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus reporting on the process and mechanisms of responses — who is involved, how interventions were implemented, and on what evidence the efforts are based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow basic principles and do's and don'ts from the guide
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide introduces the basic principles and the do's and don'ts of solutions journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the guide as a practical checklist: adopt its recommended practices, heed its cautions, and apply its examples and anti-patterns when planning and reporting solutions-driven stories.
